clusters.name: His stepfather Desmond in the home, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987, when you were fourteen and stepping into secondary school, three shifts in your relationships appeared within months: distance from Desmond, warmth toward your dad, and anxiety as you made the chess squad and found yourself out of your depth. Your stepfather's separation from your mother over a baby question sat nearby, and these months held no other shifts in the family.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return and your grandfather's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: From 1989 to early 1994, your father's father came back into the family after years away, your family moved into the rebuilt house on Hollin Road, and then your mother's father died. Within these years your anxiety and symptoms rose: late nights you were unsure about, dropping chess and debate, a wrist injury stopping your playing, a blow-up with your closest friend Rafe, getting high alone in your room. Your functioning fell as you underfunctioned on college forms and leaned hard on Rafe, then spiralled into loss and low feeling once your grandfather was gone. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in 1994, placed among these shifts. The period settles in early 1994 as you found your drive again with an exchange abroad.

clusters.name: Your split with Joelle and therapy begun, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around 1998 and 1999, a relationship of eighteen months and a separation within the year, insomnia began getting in the way of your performing though you were playing the best you ever had, winning competitions. You started with a therapist after the split. Your anxiety rose and functioning fell slightly even as your playing reached its peak; the two shifts held together in the same months, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer and death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From 2001 to early 2004, your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and underwent surgery and chemotherapy. Around the same time, you ran out of steam for performing and had a disastrous audition in your home town. You sank into a deep depression once you split with Marisol that autumn, at the bottom and hardly moving from the sofa. You were on poor terms with family and friends, distance from your parents who seemed a world away. You relied on friends—Corbin, Dale, Silas, Hamish—turned toward them and away from family. Your functioning fell, your anxiety rose. By January 2004 you had begun swimming laps, returned to your therapist Victor, and requested help from your parents with therapy costs. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home and died in February 2004. The period settles as you moved toward recovery and your parents' help.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and nursing school begun, 2008
clusters.reason: In 2008, your grandmother Lorna died and your grandfather Clifford died around the same time. You were at Alder Creek building with Silas, too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed to visit you against your wishes and the visit went wrong. You stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound that summer—a cutoff that held for roughly a year. Your anxiety rose around her visits and the conflict between you. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke that winter. Within these months, distance piled up between you and your mother as you relocated and began the nursing programme. The period settles as the year of silence held its course.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her family's upheaval, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: From your marriage to Wren in March 2017 through autumn 2019, shifts piled up in your marriage and toward her family. You saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along. Your anxiety rose as you constantly feel you ought to drive projects forward; you started a sleeping pill. Around the lake weekend for her mother's retirement in October 2019, Wren became swamped with one thing after another—a street party, a fundraising dinner, the drive to the lake. Her symptom and anxiety rose, her functioning fell. You overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her; her family talks all day, nothing happens to one that the others don't hear. Once the weekend had a plan the dinner went well and she settled. But you awoke from small hours at the lake with no more sleep, anxious when around her family, feeling you don't belong. Long quiet drives home afterward. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2017, your cousin Bella had returned to Danfield in 2019, your sister Tara was expecting her first child. The period remains open as these shifts continue.
